body.statement: There exists a finite-alphabet model \(\eta^\dagger\in\mathfrak M_{3,1}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) whose graph and target data equal \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\). For every such faithful model, \(A(\eta^\dagger)=\{1,2\}\), \(Z_1=\{3\}\), and Dai et al.'s retained-edge result gives \(1\to2\) in \(M_1(\eta^\dagger)\). Consequently, the endpoint at vertex \(2\) on that retained adjacency is an arrowhead although \(2\notin Z_1\). The corrected endpoint frontier therefore makes its arrowhead equivalence only for intervention-created adjacencies \(uv\notin H\); it makes no target-membership equivalence for retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\).
body.justification: The explicit three-variable reduction separates retained basal orientation from the target-driven orientation mechanism and removes the failed normalization.
body.gap: Dai et al., Lemma 6 on p. 7, supplies retained-edge semantics; target membership controls intervention-created adjacencies through a distinct mechanism and cannot characterize retained-edge arrowheads.
body.consumer: It gives an executable unit check for any implementation of the fixed-selected-set endpoint frontier.
